question_text: The fraction of nonreflected radiation that is transmitted through a 5-mm thickness of a transparent material is 0.95 . If the thickness is increased to 12 mm , what fraction of light will be transmitted?
response:
The transmitted (non-reflected) fraction obeys the Beer–Lambert law, $I/I_0 = e^{-\alpha x}$, so it decays exponentially with thickness.

Given $0.95 = e^{-\alpha(5\,\text{mm})}$, at $12\,\text{mm}$:

$$\frac{I}{I_0} = e^{-\alpha(12)} = \left(e^{-\alpha(5)}\right)^{12/5} = 0.95^{12/5} \approx 0.884$$

$$\boxed{0.884}$$
